name: Total External Blackbox Assessment - Domain Only
description: Fully unauthenticated, domain-in attacker-perspective assessment. Covers passive OSINT, DNS/email security, subdomain and attack-surface mapping, TLS, active scanning, cloud storage/source leak discovery, dark web intelligence, AI/LLM agent exposure (MITRE ATLAS), unauthenticated web testing, network perimeter, and social-engineering surface. No authentication, no AD assumptions - pure external attacker view.

items.name: WHOIS & Domain Registration Intelligence
mitre_technique: T1596.002 - Search Open Technical Databases: WHOIS
items.how: Enumerate registrar, registrant org, creation/expiry dates, name servers, and privacy-proxy usage to build organizational and infrastructure context.
cases: Run whois against root domain and all discovered subdomains' parent zones
Check domain expiry date for hijack-via-non-renewal risk
Identify registrar lock status (clientTransferProhibited)
Cross-reference registrant org name against known shell/holding companies
items.expected: Domain has registrar lock enabled, valid expiry >90 days out, and privacy protection enabled on registrant PII.
items.recommendation: Enable registry/registrar lock, enable WHOIS privacy, set auto-renewal, and monitor expiry via uptime/monitoring tooling.

items.name: Search Engine & Public Document OSINT
mitre_technique: T1593.002 - Search Open Websites/Domains: Search Engines
items.how: Use Google/Bing dorking and metadata harvesting to find exposed documents, internal paths, and indexed sensitive files belonging to the organization.
cases: Dork: site:{{DOMAIN}} filetype:pdf OR filetype:xlsx OR filetype:docx
Dork: site:{{DOMAIN}} intitle:index.of
Extract metadata (author, software version, internal usernames) from harvested documents
Search cached/archived pages via Wayback Machine for removed-but-indexed content
items.expected: No internal documents, credentials, or directory listings are publicly indexed.
items.recommendation: Remove sensitive indexed documents, disable directory listing, add robots.txt/noindex where appropriate, strip metadata before publishing files.

items.name: Employee & Email Format Enumeration
mitre_technique: T1589.002 - Gather Victim Identity Information: Email Addresses
items.how: Harvest employee names, roles, and email address patterns from professional networks, company pages, and public breach aggregators to build a phishing/credential-stuffing target list.
cases: Harvest emails/names via theHarvester across all public sources
Determine email naming convention (first.last@, flast@, etc.)
Identify technical/IT/security staff for targeted social engineering
Cross-check harvested emails against public breach-exposure databases (read-only enumeration)
items.expected: Email convention and staff listing findings are documented purely for risk awareness; no exploitation performed without separate written authorization for social engineering.
items.recommendation: Train staff on OSINT exposure, limit public org-chart detail, enforce MFA to blunt value of harvested email addresses.

items.name: Passive Technology Stack Fingerprinting
mitre_technique: T1592.002 - Gather Victim Host Information: Software
items.how: Use third-party aggregator APIs (not direct probing) to identify technology stack, hosting provider, and historical infrastructure changes without touching target systems.
cases: Query BuiltWith/Wappalyzer API for current and historical tech stack
Identify hosting provider / CDN from passive DNS history
Flag end-of-life or known-vulnerable software versions for later active validation
items.expected: No critically outdated or EOL software components identified in passive footprint.
items.recommendation: Maintain an internal asset/version inventory and patch cadence so externally-visible stack never trails more than one minor version behind vendor support.

items.name: DNS Zone Transfer & Record Enumeration
mitre_technique: T1590.002 - Gather Victim Network Information: DNS
items.how: Attempt zone transfers against all authoritative name servers and enumerate full record set (A/AAAA/MX/TXT/NS/SOA/SRV/CNAME).
cases: dig axfr against each NS record for the domain
Enumerate all record types via dig/dnsrecon
Check for internal hostnames or IP ranges leaked in TXT/SPF records
Identify stale or orphaned DNS entries pointing to decommissioned infrastructure
items.expected: Zone transfer is refused (REFUSED/timeout) on all name servers; no internal network data leaked via DNS records.
items.recommendation: Restrict AXFR to authorized secondary name servers only, audit and remove stale DNS records quarterly.

items.name: SPF / DKIM / DMARC Email Spoofing Assessment
mitre_technique: T1590.002 - Gather Victim Network Information: DNS
items.cvss_score: 7.5 (High) if missing/misconfigured, enables T1566 Phishing downstream
items.how: Validate presence and strictness of SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records to assess domain spoofing / phishing-impersonation risk.
cases: Resolve TXT record for SPF and verify -all (hard fail) vs ~all (soft fail) vs missing
Verify DKIM selector records exist and are RSA 2048-bit minimum
Resolve _dmarc TXT record and verify policy is p=reject or p=quarantine (not p=none)
Test actual spoofed-email delivery against a controlled mailbox (with written authorization) to confirm enforcement
items.expected: SPF ends in -all, DKIM is configured with 2048-bit keys, DMARC policy is quarantine or reject with rua/ruf reporting configured.
items.recommendation: Set SPF -all, enforce DMARC p=reject after a monitoring period at p=none/quarantine, rotate DKIM keys annually.

items.name: DNSSEC Validation & Chain of Trust Check
mitre_technique: T1590.002 - Gather Victim Network Information: DNS
items.how: Verify DNSSEC is enabled and validates correctly end-to-end to mitigate DNS cache-poisoning/spoofing risk.
cases: Query DNSKEY and RRSIG records for the domain
Validate chain of trust from root to leaf using delv or dig +dnssec
Check parent zone DS record matches child zone DNSKEY
items.expected: DNSSEC is fully enabled and validates without SERVFAIL across the chain.
items.recommendation: Enable DNSSEC at the registrar and authoritative DNS provider, monitor for signature expiry.

items.name: Subdomain Takeover via Dangling DNS Records
mitre_technique: T1190 - Exploit Public-Facing Application
items.how: Identify CNAMEs pointing to deprovisioned third-party services (S3, Azure, GitHub Pages, Heroku, etc.) that an attacker could claim and serve malicious content from the victim's own subdomain.
cases: Enumerate all CNAME records across discovered subdomains
Match CNAME targets against known vulnerable-service fingerprints (NXDOMAIN, 'bucket does not exist', etc.)
Attempt safe, non-destructive proof-of-concept claim on a sandbox/throwaway account where policy allows
Verify finding manually before reporting to avoid false positives
items.expected: No CNAME records point to unclaimed/deprovisioned third-party resources.
items.recommendation: Remove DNS records immediately when decommissioning third-party services; run automated subdomain-takeover scanning in CI/CD on every DNS change.

items.name: Passive Subdomain Enumeration
mitre_technique: T1590.002 - Gather Victim Network Information: DNS
T1596.003 - Search Open Technical Databases: Digital Certificates
items.how: Aggregate subdomains from certificate transparency logs, passive DNS databases, and public datasets without touching the target directly.
cases: Query crt.sh for all certs issued under {{DOMAIN}}
Run subfinder/amass in passive-only mode across all configured sources
Deduplicate and normalize the combined subdomain list
items.expected: Full passive subdomain inventory produced and matched against the organization's known asset register.
items.recommendation: Maintain an authoritative asset inventory and alert on newly-observed certificates/subdomains not present in it.

items.name: Active Subdomain Brute-Force & Permutation Scanning
mitre_technique: T1595.002 - Active Scanning: Vulnerability Scanning
items.how: Resolve a large permutation/brute-force wordlist against the domain's authoritative name servers to surface subdomains missing from passive sources.
cases: Run DNS brute force using a large curated wordlist (jhaddix all.txt or similar)
Generate permutations of known subdomains (dev-, staging-, old-, v2-) and resolve them
Rate-limit resolution to avoid DNS provider throttling/alerting
items.expected: Active enumeration confirms the passive list and surfaces any environment (dev/staging/uat) subdomains missing from inventory.
items.recommendation: Apply identical security controls to non-production subdomains as production, or remove public DNS entries for internal-only environments.

items.name: Live Host & HTTP Service Triage
mitre_technique: T1595.001 - Active Scanning: Scanning IP Blocks
items.how: Resolve the combined subdomain list to IPs, probe for live HTTP(S) services, and capture titles/status codes/tech stack for triage prioritization.
cases: Resolve all subdomains to IPs with dnsx
Probe HTTP/HTTPS on standard and common alternate ports (80,443,8080,8443,8000,8888)
Capture page title, status code, content-length, and tech fingerprint per live host
Flag hosts returning 401/403 (potential hidden admin panels) for manual follow-up
items.expected: Comprehensive live-host inventory with triage metadata produced for all phases downstream.
items.recommendation: Decommission or firewall unused/forgotten live hosts identified during triage.

items.name: Virtual Host / SNI Enumeration on Shared IPs
mitre_technique: T1590.005 - Gather Victim Network Information: IP Addresses
items.how: On IPs hosting multiple sites (shared hosting/load balancers), enumerate virtual hosts via SNI/Host-header fuzzing to reveal non-DNS-registered applications sharing the same IP.
cases: Fuzz Host header against discovered IPs using a vhost wordlist
Enumerate SNI certificate names bound to each shared IP
Cross-reference revealed vhosts against the known asset inventory
items.expected: No undocumented virtual hosts are discoverable on shared infrastructure IPs.
items.recommendation: Use dedicated IPs or strict default-deny vhost configuration so unregistered Host headers return a generic error, not a different application.

items.name: Certificate Transparency Log Harvesting
mitre_technique: T1596.003 - Search Open Technical Databases: Digital Certificates
items.how: Mine CT logs for every certificate issued to the domain to surface internal hostnames, pre-launch environments, and wildcard scope.
cases: Query crt.sh/censys CT log APIs for full certificate history
Identify internal-only hostnames unintentionally leaked via SAN entries
Flag wildcard certificates (*.{{DOMAIN}}) and assess their exposure blast radius
items.expected: No internal-only hostnames are exposed via public CT logs.
items.recommendation: Use internal/private CAs for non-public-facing hosts, avoid including internal hostnames in public-cert SANs.

items.name: TLS Protocol & Cipher Suite Weakness Assessment
mitre_technique: T1595.002 - Active Scanning: Vulnerability Scanning
items.cvss_score: 6.5 (Medium, higher if TLS 1.0/1.1 or export ciphers present)
items.how: Assess supported TLS versions, cipher suites, and key exchange strength for downgrade and MITM susceptibility.
cases: Scan for TLS 1.0/1.1 support (should be disabled)
Check for weak ciphers: RC4, 3DES, export-grade, NULL ciphers
Test for Heartbleed, POODLE, BEAST, CRIME, ROBOT vulnerabilities
Verify forward secrecy (ECDHE) is enforced
items.expected: Only TLS 1.2/1.3 enabled, strong AEAD ciphers only, forward secrecy enforced, no legacy vulnerabilities present.
items.recommendation: Disable TLS 1.0/1.1, remove weak/export ciphers, enforce ECDHE-based cipher suites, apply latest patches to TLS stack.

items.name: Certificate Validity, Wildcard Exposure & Mismanagement
mitre_technique: T1596.003 - Search Open Technical Databases: Digital Certificates
items.how: Validate certificate chain correctness, expiry windows, and whether wildcard certs are over-scoped relative to actual usage.
cases: Verify full chain validates to a trusted root with no intermediate gaps
Confirm expiry is >30 days out across all live hosts
Assess blast radius if a wildcard cert's private key were compromised
Check for self-signed certs on any production-facing endpoint
items.expected: All certs valid, properly chained, >30 days from expiry, and scoped as tightly as operationally feasible.
items.recommendation: Automate certificate renewal (ACME/Let's Encrypt or enterprise CA automation), prefer SAN-specific certs over broad wildcards for high-value hosts.

items.name: Full TCP/UDP Port Sweep
mitre_technique: T1595.001 - Active Scanning: Scanning IP Blocks
items.how: Perform a full 65535-port TCP sweep (plus top-1000 UDP) against all live IPs to establish the complete exposed-port baseline.
cases: Fast full-port TCP discovery scan to identify open ports
Follow with targeted -sV -sC on discovered open ports
Run top-1000 UDP scan (full UDP sweeps are slow/unreliable at scale)
items.expected: Open port set matches the documented/expected service inventory exactly - no unexpected ports open.
items.recommendation: Apply default-deny firewall rules; only explicitly required ports should ever be reachable from the internet.
items.command_template: masscan -p1-65535 {{IP}} --rate 2000 -oL masscan_out.txt && nmap -sV -sC -p$(cat masscan_out.txt | awk '{print $3}' | tr '\n' ',') {{IP}} -oA nmap_full

items.name: Service Version & Banner Enumeration
mitre_technique: T1592.002 - Gather Victim Host Information: Software
items.how: Grab service banners and version strings on every open port to feed CVE correlation and identify unnecessary information disclosure.
cases: Run nmap -sV against all open ports for version detection
Manually grab banners on non-standard ports via netcat for services nmap misidentifies
Flag services disclosing internal version/build numbers in banners
items.expected: Minimal/generic banners; internal build details not disclosed externally.
items.recommendation: Suppress or genericize service banners (server_tokens off in nginx, ServerTokens Prod in Apache, etc.).

items.name: Exposed Management & Remote Access Interfaces
mitre_technique: T1133 - External Remote Services
items.how: Specifically hunt for internet-exposed admin/management surfaces (SSH, RDP, WinRM, Redis, Elasticsearch, Jenkins, phpMyAdmin, Kubernetes API, Docker API, VNC) that should sit behind VPN.
cases: Check for exposed RDP (3389), SSH (22 with password auth), WinRM (5985/5986)
Check for unauthenticated Redis (6379), Elasticsearch (9200), MongoDB (27017), Kubernetes API (6443/8443)
Identify exposed CI/CD consoles (Jenkins 8080, GitLab Runner) reachable without VPN
Attempt safe banner/version check only - do NOT attempt exploitation on critical infra without explicit scoping sign-off
items.expected: No administrative/management interface is reachable from the open internet; all require VPN or IP-allowlist access.
items.recommendation: Move all management interfaces behind VPN/bastion with MFA, enforce IP allowlisting at the firewall, disable password auth on SSH in favor of key-based auth.

items.name: Known CVE Correlation via Automated Templates
mitre_technique: T1595.002 - Active Scanning: Vulnerability Scanning
items.cvss_score: Varies per matched CVE (report actual CVSS of each finding)
items.how: Correlate fingerprinted service/software versions against current CVE databases using signature-based vulnerability scanning templates.
cases: Run nuclei CVE template set against all live hosts
Cross-reference nmap NSE vuln scripts output against NVD/Vulners
Prioritize validation of any CVE with a public PoC/known-exploited-vulnerabilities (CISA KEV) listing
items.expected: No unpatched CVE-matched vulnerabilities present, especially none on the CISA KEV list.
items.recommendation: Establish a patch SLA tied to CVSS/KEV status (e.g., KEV items patched within 72 hours), automate CVE scanning in CI.
items.command_template: nuclei -l live_hosts.txt -t cves/ -t vulnerabilities/ -severity critical,high,medium -o nuclei_cve_results.txt

items.name: CMS / Framework / Server Identification
mitre_technique: T1592.002 - Gather Victim Host Information: Software
items.how: Fingerprint CMS platforms, backend frameworks, and web servers to target version-specific vulnerability research.
cases: Run whatweb/wappalyzer against each live host
Check for CMS-specific files (wp-login.php, /administrator, sitecore, etc.)
Identify backend framework via error pages, header leakage (X-Powered-By), and response fingerprints
items.expected: Identified stack versions are current/supported; no End-of-Life CMS or framework in use.
items.recommendation: Keep CMS/plugins/frameworks on vendor-supported versions, suppress version-disclosing headers (X-Powered-By, Server).

items.name: WAF / CDN Detection & Bypass Feasibility
mitre_technique: T1590.004 - Gather Victim Network Information: Network Topology
items.how: Determine whether a WAF/CDN sits in front of the origin, and assess whether the real origin IP can be discovered to bypass WAF protection entirely.
cases: Fingerprint WAF vendor via response headers/behavior (wafw00f)
Attempt origin-IP discovery via historical DNS (SecurityTrails/passive DNS), SSL cert SAN matching, and subdomain misconfig (e.g. direct-connect subdomains bypassing CDN)
If origin found, verify whether origin firewall accepts direct traffic (bypassing WAF protections entirely)
items.expected: True origin IP is not discoverable, or if discovered, origin firewall only accepts traffic from the CDN/WAF IP ranges.
items.recommendation: Lock origin server firewall to only accept connections from CDN/WAF provider IP ranges, rotate origin IP if previously exposed, avoid exposing origin IP via subdomains or mail/DNS records.

items.name: Client-Side JavaScript Library & Dependency Exposure
mitre_technique: T1592.002 - Gather Victim Host Information: Software
items.how: Enumerate client-side JS libraries and their versions to identify known-vulnerable dependencies (e.g. outdated jQuery, Angular, Lodash with public XSS/prototype-pollution CVEs).
cases: Crawl rendered pages and extract all loaded JS library versions
Match versions against Retire.js/Snyk vulnerability database
Review source maps (.map files) for accidental source code exposure
items.expected: No client-side library in use has a known critical/high CVE; source maps are not exposed in production.
items.recommendation: Keep front-end dependencies patched via automated dependency scanning in CI, strip source maps from production builds.

items.name: Public S3 / Azure Blob / GCS Bucket Discovery
mitre_technique: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage
items.how: Enumerate cloud storage buckets related to the organization's brand/domain naming conventions and test for public read/write/list permissions.
cases: Permute bucket names from domain/brand/product names (company, company-backup, company-dev, etc.)
Check each candidate bucket for public List, Read, and Write ACL permissions
If public, sample (do not exfiltrate bulk data) file listing to assess sensitivity of exposed content
Repeat across AWS S3, Azure Blob Storage, and GCS naming conventions
items.expected: No cloud storage buckets are publicly listable, readable, or writable; access requires authenticated/signed requests only.
items.recommendation: Enable S3 Block Public Access account-wide, apply least-privilege bucket policies, enable access logging and alerting on ACL changes.

items.name: Serverless / API Gateway Endpoint Exposure
mitre_technique: T1595.002 - Active Scanning: Vulnerability Scanning
items.how: Identify exposed serverless functions (Lambda URLs, Azure Functions, Cloud Functions) and API Gateway stages that may bypass intended auth layers.
cases: Discover *.execute-api.*.amazonaws.com, *.azurewebsites.net, *.cloudfunctions.net endpoints linked to the domain
Test discovered endpoints for missing authentication/authorization on invocation
Check for verbose error messages leaking stack traces, internal IPs, or environment variables
items.expected: All serverless/API gateway endpoints require authentication; no verbose errors leak internal infrastructure detail.
items.recommendation: Require API keys/IAM auth on all gateway stages, disable verbose stack traces in production, enable WAF on API Gateway.

items.name: Exposed CI/CD Pipelines & Artifact Repositories
mitre_technique: T1195.002 - Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
items.how: Identify internet-reachable CI/CD dashboards, container registries, and artifact repositories that could allow supply-chain compromise if accessed.
cases: Discover exposed Jenkins, GitLab CI, TeamCity, or CircleCI dashboards
Check for unauthenticated Docker registry (v2/_catalog endpoint) exposure
Check for exposed Nexus/Artifactory/npm private registries without auth
items.expected: No CI/CD dashboard or artifact registry is reachable without authentication from the internet.
items.recommendation: Place all CI/CD and registry infrastructure behind VPN/SSO, enforce authentication on all registry API endpoints.

items.name: GitHub / GitLab Dork & Secret Scanning
mitre_technique: T1552.001 - Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files
items.how: Search public code repositories and commit history for hardcoded credentials, API keys, and internal configuration belonging to the organization.
cases: Dork GitHub/GitLab for the domain, brand name, and known internal project names
Scan matched repos/commit history with TruffleHog/Gitleaks for secret patterns (AWS keys, private keys, JWT secrets, DB connection strings)
Check for forked/deleted-but-cached repos that still expose historical secrets
Validate (read-only, non-destructive) whether any discovered key is still active before reporting severity
items.expected: No live organizational secrets are present in public repositories or commit history.
items.recommendation: Rotate any discovered credential immediately, add pre-commit secret-scanning hooks, run gitleaks/trufflehog in CI on every push, purge secrets from git history with BFG/filter-repo.

items.name: Paste-Site & Public Code-Sharing Credential Monitoring
mitre_technique: T1552.001 - Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files
items.how: Search Pastebin-style sites and public code-sharing platforms for accidental dumps of config files, credentials, or internal data referencing the domain.
cases: Query Pastebin/Ghostbin/Gist search for domain and brand-related keywords
Search PSBDMP (Pastebin dump search engine) historical archive
Flag any config/credential dump and trace back to likely leak source (developer laptop, misconfigured CI log, etc.)
items.expected: No current organizational secrets or internal configuration are found on public paste platforms.
items.recommendation: Subscribe to a continuous paste-site monitoring feed (e.g., via breach-intel vendor) tied to brand/domain keywords for ongoing detection.

items.name: Exposed .git / .env / Backup File Discovery
mitre_technique: T1552.001 - Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files
items.how: Probe each live host for accidentally-deployed version-control directories, environment files, and backup archives directly reachable over HTTP.
cases: Request /.git/HEAD and /.git/config on all live hosts; if 200 OK, attempt (non-destructive) dump via git-dumper for evidence
Request /.env, /.env.bak, /config.php.bak, /wp-config.php.bak and similar common backup patterns
Fuzz for common backup archive names (backup.zip, site.tar.gz, db_dump.sql)
items.expected: No version control metadata, environment files, or backup archives are reachable over HTTP on any live host.
items.recommendation: Exclude dotfiles and backup extensions at the web server/reverse-proxy level, never deploy .git directories to production webroots, store secrets in a vault service rather than .env files on web-accessible paths.

items.name: Dark Web Marketplace & Forum Mention Monitoring
mitre_technique: T1597.002 - Search Closed Sources: Purchase Technical Data
items.cvss_score: N/A (Intelligence Finding) - severity scales with data sold/offered
items.how: Search dark web marketplaces, hacking forums, and Telegram channels for mentions of the organization, its domain, or employees being sold, discussed, or targeted. Note: open-source dark web tooling has materially weaker coverage than commercial threat-intel platforms - see gap analysis.
cases: Search known onion-indexed forums/marketplaces for domain/brand mentions via Tor-routed queries
Monitor Telegram channels known for initial-access-broker (IAB) listings for the organization's name/sector
Document any listing offering access, credentials, or data purportedly from the organization (do not purchase/interact with sellers)
items.expected: No active listings offering unauthorized access to, or data from, the organization.
items.recommendation: If a credible listing is found, escalate immediately to incident response outside the pentest scope; consider a paid dark-web monitoring subscription for continuous coverage (see gap analysis).

items.name: Credential Breach Database Correlation
mitre_technique: T1589.001 - Gather Victim Identity Information: Credentials
items.cvss_score: 7.5 (High) scaled by number of live/reused credentials found
items.how: Check harvested organizational email addresses against known breach-compilation databases to assess password-reuse and credential-stuffing risk.
cases: Query Have I Been Pwned (domain search, if domain verified) for breach exposure count
Cross-check harvested employee emails against Dehashed/Intelligence X for plaintext/hash exposure
Assess whether exposed passwords follow a pattern suggesting reuse across corporate accounts (do not attempt login with found credentials without explicit authorization)
items.expected: Exposure found is historical/third-party only; no evidence of current corporate credential reuse.
items.recommendation: Enforce MFA everywhere to blunt reuse risk, run continuous breach-monitoring on corporate domain, enforce password-manager usage and periodic forced resets after confirmed exposure.

items.name: Ransomware Leak-Site Exposure Check
mitre_technique: T1597.002 - Search Closed Sources: Purchase Technical Data
items.cvss_score: N/A (Intelligence Finding) - treat any hit as critical/incident-level
items.how: Check known ransomware-group leak sites and aggregator trackers for any listing referencing the organization, indicating prior or ongoing compromise.
cases: Search ransomware leak-site aggregator trackers (e.g. ransomwatch, ransomlook) for domain/brand mentions
If a listing exists, document URL/date/group without downloading any leaked data
Correlate listing date against known organizational incidents if any
items.expected: No listing referencing the organization exists on any tracked ransomware leak site.
items.recommendation: Any positive hit must be escalated immediately to incident response leadership - this is outside normal pentest finding remediation and requires IR activation.

phases.name: AI / LLM Agent Exposure Scanning (MITRE ATLAS)

items.name: Exposed LLM API Endpoint Discovery
mitre_technique: AML.T0000 - Search for Victim's Publicly Available Research Materials (ATLAS analogue)
items.how: ATT&CK has no native technique for this - use MITRE ATLAS (AI-specific adversarial framework) as the reference model. Identify internet-reachable AI chat/inference endpoints tied to the organization and test for missing authentication/rate limiting.
cases: Discover endpoints matching /v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions, /api/chat, /predict patterns via nuclei/httpx
Probe for Ollama (port 11434), Text-Generation-Inference, vLLM, or LocalAI default endpoints exposed externally
Test whether inference endpoints require API-key authentication or are fully open
Check for exposed model-serving dashboards (e.g. Triton Inference Server, BentoML) without auth
items.expected: No LLM/inference endpoint is reachable without authentication; rate limiting is enforced to prevent resource-exhaustion abuse.
items.recommendation: Require API-key/OAuth auth on all inference endpoints, place model-serving infra behind the same perimeter controls as any other internal API, enforce per-key rate limits.

items.name: Vector Database & Embedding Store Exposure
mitre_technique: AML.T0024 - Exfiltration via ML Inference API (ATLAS analogue)
items.cvss_score: 8.2 (High) if embeddings containing sensitive source data are extractable
items.how: Vector databases backing RAG/AI-agent features can leak the underlying proprietary documents via embedding similarity queries if left unauthenticated. Identify and test exposure of Pinecone/Weaviate/Milvus/Qdrant/Chroma instances.
cases: Scan for default ports of common vector DBs (Weaviate 8080, Milvus 19530, Qdrant 6333, Chroma 8000) reachable externally
Test for unauthenticated query/list-collections access on discovered instances
If accessible, assess (without bulk-extracting) whether raw source text is retrievable from embeddings, not just vector values
items.expected: No vector database instance is reachable or queryable without authentication from the internet.
items.recommendation: Never expose vector DB ports directly to the internet; require API-key/mTLS auth and place behind the application's own auth layer, not the DB's default (often none).
tools: shodan (port:19530 OR port:6333 OR port:8080 product filters)

items.name: Prompt Injection & Jailbreak Susceptibility of Public-Facing AI Features
mitre_technique: AML.T0051 - LLM Prompt Injection (ATLAS)
items.cvss_score: 6.4 (Medium, higher if injection enables data exfiltration or tool/function-calling abuse)
items.how: If the organization exposes a public-facing chatbot or AI agent, test it for direct/indirect prompt-injection that bypasses system-prompt restrictions or triggers unintended tool/function calls. Manual, expert-driven testing - no mature CLI tooling exists for this yet (see gap analysis).
cases: Attempt direct prompt injection to reveal system prompt or bypass stated restrictions
If the agent has tool-calling/function-calling capability, test whether injected instructions can trigger unintended external actions
Test indirect injection via content the agent is asked to summarize/process (e.g. a webpage or document containing hidden instructions)
Assess whether the agent can be coerced into leaking other users' conversation data or internal configuration
items.expected: System prompt and restrictions hold under adversarial input; tool-calling is strictly scoped and cannot be redirected by injected content.
items.recommendation: Apply input/output filtering layers independent of the LLM itself, strictly scope what tools/functions an agent can invoke and require explicit confirmation for sensitive actions, never place long-term secrets directly in the system prompt.

items.name: AI Model Supply Chain & Inference Infrastructure Exposure
mitre_technique: AML.T0010 - ML Supply Chain Compromise (ATLAS)
items.how: Identify whether the organization pulls models from unverified/public sources (HuggingFace, public model hubs) without integrity verification, and whether model-loading infrastructure is externally reachable.
cases: Identify any public references (job postings, GitHub, docs) to which model hub/source is used for production inference
Check whether model-serving infra validates model checksums/signatures before loading (requires architecture-review input, not purely external testing)
Scan for exposed model-management dashboards (MLflow, Kubeflow) reachable externally
items.expected: Models are pulled from verified/internal registries with integrity checks; no model-management dashboard is externally reachable without auth.
items.recommendation: Pin model versions by verified hash, mirror approved models into an internal registry rather than pulling directly from public hubs at runtime, authenticate all ML-ops tooling dashboards.

items.name: Unauthenticated OWASP Top 10 Sweep
mitre_technique: T1190 - Exploit Public-Facing Application
items.how: Run automated and manual testing for the OWASP Top 10 against every publicly reachable endpoint that does not require authentication (contact forms, search, public APIs, password-reset flows, etc.).
cases: Test all input parameters for reflected/stored XSS
Test all query/body parameters for SQL injection (error-based, boolean, time-based, UNION)
Test any endpoint accepting URLs/file paths for SSRF (cloud metadata endpoint as canary: 169.254.169.254)
Test public password-reset/forgot-password flow for username enumeration and token predictability
items.expected: No critical/high OWASP Top 10 vulnerability is exploitable without authentication.
items.recommendation: Use parameterized queries, context-aware output encoding, an allowlist-based SSRF guard on any server-side URL fetch, and generic (non-enumerable) responses on auth-adjacent flows.

items.name: Default Credential & Exposed Login Panel Discovery
mitre_technique: T1078.001 - Valid Accounts: Default Accounts
items.how: Discover all externally-reachable login panels (admin, CMS, device management) and test against known default credential lists with strict lockout-aware rate limiting.
cases: Enumerate all discoverable login/admin panels across live hosts
Test a small, curated default-credential list per identified platform (never a full brute-force without written rate-limit authorization)
Check whether account lockout/rate-limiting is enforced after failed attempts
items.expected: No default/vendor credentials succeed; account lockout triggers after a small number of failed attempts.
items.recommendation: Force credential change on first login for all admin/device accounts, enforce account lockout and progressive delay, monitor for credential-stuffing patterns.

items.name: Public API Endpoint Discovery & Unauthenticated Access Testing
mitre_technique: T1190 - Exploit Public-Facing Application
items.how: Discover REST/GraphQL API endpoints behind the public web app and test whether any sensitive operation is reachable without authentication or via broken object-level authorization (BOLA/IDOR) at the unauthenticated layer.
cases: Crawl JS bundles for API route definitions and Swagger/OpenAPI spec files
Fuzz discovered REST routes for endpoints missing auth middleware
Test GraphQL introspection exposure (should be disabled in production)
Test sequential/predictable ID parameters for IDOR even pre-authentication (e.g. public order-tracking, invoice-lookup pages)
items.expected: No sensitive API operation is reachable without authentication; GraphQL introspection disabled in production.
items.recommendation: Enforce authentication/authorization middleware on every route by default (deny-by-default), disable GraphQL introspection in production, use non-sequential opaque identifiers for any public-facing lookup.

items.name: Unrestricted File Upload on Public-Facing Forms
mitre_technique: T1190 - Exploit Public-Facing Application
items.cvss_score: 9.8 (Critical) if executable upload leads to RCE
items.how: Test any public-facing upload feature (CV/resume uploads, support-ticket attachments, image uploads) for insufficient file-type/content validation that could allow web-shell upload.
cases: Attempt upload of disguised executable content (double extension, null-byte, content-type spoofing, polyglot files)
Verify uploaded files are stored outside the web-executable directory or served with safe Content-Disposition/Content-Type headers
Test whether uploaded file path is predictable/guessable for direct retrieval
items.expected: Upload functionality strictly validates file type/content (not just extension), stores files outside the executable webroot, and serves them with forced-download headers.
items.recommendation: Validate file content via magic-byte/MIME inspection server-side, store uploads outside the webroot or in object storage with no execute permission, randomize stored filenames.

items.name: Business Logic Abuse on Public Forms (Account Enumeration / Rate-Limit Bypass)
mitre_technique: T1589.001 - Gather Victim Identity Information: Credentials
items.how: Test public login, registration, and password-reset forms for response-timing or messaging differences that allow attacker-side account/email enumeration, and test whether rate-limiting can be bypassed.
cases: Compare response time/message for valid vs invalid usernames on login/reset forms
Test rate-limit bypass via header manipulation (X-Forwarded-For rotation) or IP rotation
Test CAPTCHA bypass feasibility (reuse of tokens, missing server-side validation)
items.expected: Identical response time/messaging regardless of account validity; rate-limiting cannot be trivially bypassed via header spoofing.
items.recommendation: Return generic responses for valid/invalid identifiers, implement server-side rate-limiting keyed on multiple signals (not just client-supplied IP headers), validate CAPTCHA tokens server-side with single-use enforcement.

items.name: IP Range / ASN Attack Surface Mapping
mitre_technique: T1590.005 - Gather Victim Network Information: IP Addresses
items.how: Map the organization's full owned ASN/IP-block footprint (not just the tested domain) to surface forgotten infrastructure sharing the same ownership.
cases: Identify ASN(s) associated with the organization via BGP/WHOIS lookups
Enumerate all IP ranges announced under the identified ASN(s)
Cross-reference against the documented asset inventory to flag undocumented IP space
items.expected: All IP space under the organization's ASN is accounted for in the asset inventory with assigned ownership/purpose.
items.recommendation: Maintain an ASN/IP-range inventory synced with the asset register, periodically re-run ASN-wide discovery to catch drift.

items.name: Edge/CDN Origin IP Disclosure
mitre_technique: T1590.005 - Gather Victim Network Information: IP Addresses
items.cvss_score: 7.5 (High) - direct origin access bypasses all WAF/CDN protection
items.how: Specifically hunt for the true origin IP behind CDN/WAF protection via historical DNS, mail server records, and misconfigured direct-access subdomains, then verify whether the origin accepts non-CDN traffic.
cases: Check historical/passive DNS (SecurityTrails, ViewDNS) for pre-CDN-migration origin records
Check MX/mail-related subdomains, which are often not proxied through the web CDN and can leak the real hosting IP block
Attempt direct Host-header connection to any candidate origin IP to confirm it serves the same application
items.expected: Origin IP cannot be discovered via passive means, or if discovered, direct connection attempts are rejected by the origin firewall.
items.recommendation: Restrict origin firewall to CDN provider IP ranges only, rotate origin IP after any suspected exposure, ensure mail and other non-web subdomains don't share the same IP as the protected web origin.

items.name: Third-Party Dependency & Supply-Chain Mapping
mitre_technique: T1591.002 - Gather Victim Org Information: Business Relationships
items.how: Catalog every third-party service the external-facing stack depends on (CDN, payment gateway, analytics, chat widgets, font/script CDNs) as each represents a supply-chain trust boundary.
cases: Enumerate all third-party domains loaded by the public website (scripts, iframes, fonts, trackers)
Assess subresource-integrity (SRI) usage on third-party script tags
Flag any third-party script loaded without SRI that has write access to the page's DOM/cookies
items.expected: All third-party scripts critical to the page are loaded with Subresource Integrity hashes, or risk is formally accepted.
items.recommendation: Add SRI attributes to third-party script tags, minimize the number of third-party origins with page-level trust, apply a strict Content-Security-Policy.

items.name: Typosquatting & Lookalike Domain Detection
mitre_technique: T1583.001 - Acquire Infrastructure: Domains
items.cvss_score: 7.5 (High) if active phishing infra found on a lookalike
items.how: Generate domain permutations (typosquats, homoglyphs, alternate TLDs) of the organization's domain and check which are registered and whether they host active phishing content.
cases: Generate permutations (character swap, omission, homoglyph, TLD variation) of {{DOMAIN}}
Resolve each permutation and check for active hosting/MX records
For resolved domains, check for phishing-kit indicators (cloned login pages, brand logos)
items.expected: No actively-hosted lookalike domain is serving phishing content impersonating the organization.
items.recommendation: Defensively register high-risk permutations, enable continuous typosquat monitoring, submit confirmed phishing domains for takedown.

items.name: Active Phishing Campaign Detection Against the Brand
mitre_technique: T1586.002 - Compromise Accounts: Email Accounts
items.cvss_score: 9.0 (Critical) if an active campaign is impersonating the brand/customers in real time
items.how: Check threat-intel phishing feeds and certificate-transparency logs for recently-issued certificates on domains impersonating the brand, which often precede or accompany active phishing campaigns.
cases: Monitor CT logs for new certificates containing the brand name on non-owned domains
Query OpenPhish/PhishTank feeds for current listings referencing the organization
Document any active campaign for takedown/legal escalation outside pentest scope
items.expected: No active phishing campaign targeting customers/employees under the organization's brand is currently live.
items.recommendation: Subscribe to a brand-protection/takedown service for continuous monitoring, pre-establish a takedown escalation path with registrars/hosting providers.

items.name: Social Media & Public Post Attack-Surface Review
mitre_technique: T1593.001 - Search Open Websites/Domains: Social Media
items.how: Review employee and corporate social media presence for internal information disclosure (badge photos, screen contents, org-chart details, internal tool names) usable for social engineering.
cases: Search for employee posts showing internal tooling, badges, or office layout
Review corporate social accounts for accidental internal-detail disclosure in posted screenshots
Identify job postings disclosing specific internal tech stack/versions useful to an attacker
items.expected: No internal-detail disclosure sufficient to materially aid social engineering or technical targeting is found.
items.recommendation: Include social-media OPSEC in security awareness training, review job postings for unnecessary internal technical detail before publishing.
